PBS Kids — POV: You forgot these defined your childhood 📼 #nostalgia #90skids #shorts

short // Apr 12, 2026 · Updated Sep 24, 2026

Watch on YouTube

The nostalgia just hit me like a truck.

This short is a montage of PBS Kids shows from back in the day, the ones a lot of us used to run home from school to watch, from Wishbone to Ghostwriter. We forget how much these shows shaped us. They were teaching us to read, solve problems and get curious, and we thought we were just watching TV.

Wishbone

A Jack Russell terrier who imagined himself as the hero of classic books. In every episode of Wishbone, something in his everyday life reminded him of a story, and suddenly he was Sherlock Holmes, Robin Hood or a character from Shakespeare. In costume. As a dog.

It sounds ridiculous, and it was. It also got a lot of kids to read Oliver Twist and The Odyssey without realizing they were doing homework.

Ghostwriter

Ghostwriter was a mystery show about a group of kids in Brooklyn who solved cases with help from a ghost nobody could see or hear. The only way the ghost could communicate was by moving letters and words around: on signs, on computer screens, in books.

So the whole show was secretly about reading and writing. And it worked, because it was genuinely tense and fun. The team, the pens on necklaces, the "Rally!" messages: if you know, you know. It even got a reboot on Apple TV+ in 2019.

The rest of the lineup

Those two weren't alone. That era of PBS was stacked: Arthur, The Magic School Bus, Reading Rainbow, Bill Nye the Science Guy, Zoom, and Barney for the little ones. The PBS Kids brand itself launched in 1999, but for a lot of us, the golden age was already well underway.

Why these shows hit different

These shows weren't trying to keep you watching. They were trying to send you somewhere else: to the library, to a book, outside to try an experiment. No algorithm, no autoplay. Just a show, then the next show, then dinner.

That's probably why they stick with us. They weren't content. They were part of growing up.

Quick answers

What was Wishbone about? A Jack Russell terrier who imagined himself as characters from classic literature, like Sherlock Holmes and Robin Hood. It aired on PBS in the '90s.

What was Ghostwriter about? A group of Brooklyn kids who solved mysteries with help from a ghost who could only communicate by rearranging written words.

When did Ghostwriter first air? On PBS, starting in 1992.

What shows were on PBS for kids in the '90s? Favorites included Wishbone, Ghostwriter, Arthur, The Magic School Bus, Reading Rainbow, Bill Nye the Science Guy and Barney & Friends.

Which PBS Kids show was your favorite, and who did you use to watch it with? Tell me in the comments.
